_units: volume_l = litres, mass_kg = kilograms, capacity_l = storage added when worn. Plate *_vox sizes are 1 cm voxels. Armor: rating = level on Ballistics.LEVELS; material = ceramic, steel, polyethylene or composite; durability divides the integrity each hit takes (ArmorRules.INTEGRITY_LOSS); plate fits = carrier tiers it fits. Carriers (aramid soft armor): soft_rating, soft_faces (front, back, side), soft_parts (chest, abdomen), spall_cover (neck, face, arms). Magazines name their round in data/rounds.json; muzzle_velocity_mps overrides the round's for that barrel. Medical: treats = wound kinds it fixes, treat_s = seconds to apply (self_mult on yourself), rushed_s / remove_s = a rushed tourniquet and taking one off. Kits (IFAK, trauma kit) hold contents (item id: count); an opened kit keeps what is left in its state. Ammo: magazines and loose rounds (stats.loose) of the same calibre go together; volume_l and mass_kg of loose rounds are per round (packed), a magazine's mass_kg is full and empty_mass_kg empty. Guns: spread_deg is the weapon's own mechanical cone (a player's aim adds the rest: Soldier.SHOOTER_*), ai_spread_deg the cone the AI shoots with (its accuracy as before P0362), rail = it takes an optic (back-up irons with none), optic = the optic it comes with; the weapon's state's optic names the one mounted (empty for none; missing: its own). Optics (type optic, P0362) mount on a rail and go with the gun: view = open (the reticle over an open sight: red dot, holographic) or tube (the scope picture, its eyepiece ring = ring, a share of the screen's height); reticle = dot, holo, lpvo, chevron or mil_dot; dot_moa and ring_moa = a lit dot's and a holographic ring's size; magnification = its power, the lowest of a variable one (1 = none), magnification_max (the mouse wheel zooms), magnification_start; power is against the unaimed view (10x = a tenth of its tangent); magnifier = a flip-up magnifier's power (the magnifier key); bdc = [range m, mils below the aim point] holds; art = its model (VoxelArt). Smoke grenades name their cloud colour in smoke_colour (SmokeCloud.COLOURS). MOLLE: a carrier's molle lists its attach points (id; type mag, pistol, knife, radio, medical or utility; at = torso-local surface point in metres; face front, back, left or right). An attachable item names the point types it fits in attach. A pouch holds what accepts lists (item ids, type:x, tag:x; anything when absent) up to max_units and/or capacity_l litres (items of up to max_item_l each). People (PeopleLayer): zip cuffs take cuff_s to put on; intel items (type intel) carry an intel kind and a proposed intel_value, and each piece found gets its own intel_id in its state. Every item has desc (one or two plain sentences: what it is) and uses (short lines: what it is for and how to use it in this game, from the code), shown in-game by ItemInfo (Captain, 2026-10-14). Rarity: stats.rarity (common, uncommon, rare or very_rare) = how often it turns up in the loot tables (data/loot_tables.json: the commonest tier of any table that holds it; an item found nowhere gets a price band), shown by ItemInfo; none on mission objects and actions (Captain, 2026-10-20). Consumables (type consumable, Consumables): consume = {drug (a WoundModel.DRUGS id: caffeine, ibuprofen, paracetamol, water, ration), doses} or {battery: true} (a fresh NVG battery). Food and water values (survival's metabolism, Needs; docs/survival_medical.md section 1): kcal, protein, carbs and fat in grams, vitamins {C, D, iron} in % of a day's need, water_l litres, spoils_days (shelf life: tins slow, fresh fast; spoiling is phase B), raw (raw meat and untreated water can make you sick), quality (water: clean, questionable or dirty; an entry's state.quality overrides it once treated). Barter (type barter): found and sold, no use yet. Salvage counts as material for rebel upgrades; workshop_credit = dollars it takes off a motor pool repair from the stash. Concealment: conceal_mult = how much longer the enemy takes to spot you prone or crouched while you carry it. Shotguns: pellet_spread_deg = the cone each buckshot pellet leaves in round its shot.

uses: Pick it with Shift+G, then G fires every block and claymore you armed on a detonator within 400 m
Linked charges (det cord) go with them

items.name: Thermite Grenade (incendiary)

stats._proposed: fuse_s, burn_s and burn_m are Proposed (Demolitions)

items.desc: An incendiary grenade set on a target: it burns white-hot through metal for a few seconds.
uses: Pick it with Shift+G, then G shows where it goes (within 2.5 m); Fire sets it on a vehicle, a gun, a cache or the ground
Lights after 3 s and burns 8 s with a bright glow and a hiss
Burnt through, a vehicle's engine is gone and it catches fire; a static gun is wrecked; a cache it's on is destroyed
Burns anyone within a metre of it

items.name: M18 Claymore

stats._proposed: cone_deg, frag_m, frag_wounds, the tripwire and arm_s are Proposed (Demolitions)

items.desc: A directional anti-personnel mine: a fan of steel balls thrown forward, aimed where you face.
uses: Pick it with Shift+G, then G shows it on the ground in front of you, facing where you look; R picks clacker, tripwire or det cord; Fire sets it
Fired by a clacker or remote (Shift+G, then G), or by anyone walking into its tripwire 2 m in front (it arms after 10 s)
Fragments wound in a 60 degree fan out to 50 m in front; behind it only the blast close by
Friendly fire: it hits whoever is in front. Your own show on the map
Left Ctrl at one you can see: pick it up again

items.name: AP Mine (pressure)

stats._proposed: trigger_m, arm_s and the blast are Proposed (Demolitions)

items.desc: A small buried anti-personnel blast mine set off by a foot or a wheel on it.
uses: Pick it with Shift+G, then G shows it on the ground in front of you; Fire buries it there
Arms after 15 s; then anyone who steps on it (friend or foe) or a vehicle rolling over it sets it off
Wrecks the leg that stepped on it and wounds those close by. Your own show on the map
Left Ctrl at a mine you can see: pick it up again

items.name: Chem Light (Green)
items.desc: A snap-and-shake glow stick: a soft green light for marking.
uses: Pick it with Shift+G, G takes it in hand: Fire throws it, Aim drops it close
Glows for 30 minutes; much brighter through night vision
Marks an LZ, a cleared room or a casualty (it sticks with whoever it lands on)

items.name: Chem Light (Red)
items.desc: A snap-and-shake glow stick: a soft red light for marking.
uses: Pick it with Shift+G, G takes it in hand: Fire throws it, Aim drops it close
Glows for 30 minutes; much brighter through night vision
Marks an LZ, a cleared room or a casualty

items.name: Chem Light (Blue)
items.desc: A snap-and-shake glow stick: a soft blue light for marking.
uses: Pick it with Shift+G, G takes it in hand: Fire throws it, Aim drops it close
Glows for 30 minutes; much brighter through night vision
Marks an LZ, a cleared room or a casualty

items.name: Chem Light (IR)
items.desc: An infrared glow stick: dark to the eye, bright through night vision.
uses: Pick it with Shift+G, G takes it in hand: Fire throws it, Aim drops it close
Seen only through night vision, for 30 minutes
Marks an LZ or a room without showing the enemy a light

items.name: Electronics Salvage
items.desc: Salvaged electronics: radios, boards and wiring worth money to the company.
uses: Carry it out and it goes to the company stash
Left in the field it counts toward the debrief's salvage pool
Salvaging a vehicle wreck yields some

items.name: M2HB (gun, packed)
items.desc: The M2 .50 machine gun off its tripod, receiver and barrel: one man's load.
uses: Heavy: 38 kg, carried in both hands; the tripod is a second man's load
With the M3 tripod within 3 m (a squadmate's hands or the ground): Left Ctrl + Left Alt (yourself) > Set up the gun, 20 s, holding still
At a set-up gun with nobody on it: Pack up the gun, 15 s

items.name: M3 Tripod (packed)
items.desc: The M2's folding tripod with its traversing and elevating gear.
uses: Heavy: 20 kg, carried in both hands
Set up with the M2's gun within 3 m: Left Ctrl + Left Alt (yourself) > Set up the gun

items.name: 60 mm Mortar Round (HE)
items.desc: A 60 mm high-explosive mortar round for the M224.
uses: Carry it, or load it into the mortar's hold
At the mortar: Lay and fire (firing table) fires one, from the hold or your kit

items.name: 82 mm Mortar Round (HE)
items.desc: An 82 mm high-explosive mortar round for the 2B14.
uses: At the mortar: Lay and fire (firing table) fires one, from the hold or your kit

items.name: M224 Tube (packed)
items.desc: The M224 60 mm mortar's tube and sight: one man's load.
uses: 9 kg, carried in both hands; the bipod and baseplate are a second man's load
With the mount within 3 m: Left Ctrl + Left Alt (yourself) > Set up the gun, 20 s

items.name: M224 Bipod and Baseplate (packed)
items.desc: The M224's bipod and baseplate.
uses: 12 kg, carried in both hands
Set up with the tube within 3 m

items.name: 2B14 Tube (packed)
items.desc: The 2B14 82 mm mortar's tube.
uses: 14 kg; the bipod and the baseplate are two more men's loads

items.name: 2B14 Bipod (packed)
items.desc: The 2B14's bipod and sight.
uses: 13 kg

items.name: 2B14 Baseplate (packed)
items.desc: The 2B14's round baseplate.
uses: 15 kg

items.name: DShK (gun, packed)
items.desc: A DShK 12.7 mm machine gun off its mount: one man's load.
uses: Heavy: 34 kg, carried in both hands; the mount is a second man's load
With the mount within 3 m: Left Ctrl + Left Alt (yourself) > Set up the gun, 20 s

items.name: DShK Tripod (packed)
items.desc: The DShK's heavy tripod mount.
uses: Heavy: 30 kg, carried in both hands
Set up with the DShK's gun within 3 m: Left Ctrl + Left Alt (yourself) > Set up the gun

items.name: HVT Hard Case
items.desc: A locked hard case a contract may want brought out.
uses: Bulky: carried in both hands (Left Ctrl > Pick up); no room in packs
Left Ctrl + Left Alt (yourself) > Drop held item sets it down
Bring it to extraction when a contract asks for it

items.name: ID Papers (proof)
items.desc: A target's identity papers, taken off his body: the client's proof of the kill.
uses: Search a killed HVT's body for it (Left Ctrl on the body > Loot)
Carry it out at extraction: an HVT kill pays in full only with it

items.name: Flight Recorder
items.desc: A downed aircraft's flight recorder (the black box) in its armoured case, still bolted to a piece of its rack.
uses: Heavy: carried in both hands (Left Ctrl > Pick up); no room in packs
Left Ctrl + Left Alt (yourself) > Drop held item sets it down
Bring it to extraction when a crash site contract asks for it

items.name: Crew ID Tags
items.desc: The identity tags of a downed aircraft's crew, gathered at the wreck.
uses: Pick them up at the crash site (Left Ctrl > Pick up)
Carry them out at extraction: a crash site contract pays a bonus for them

items.name: Supply Crate
items.desc: A crate of supplies, too big for any pack.
uses: Bulky: carried in both hands (Left Ctrl > Pick up)
Can be loaded into a vehicle's hold
Left Ctrl + Left Alt (yourself) > Drop held item sets it down

items.name: Supply Pallet
items.desc: A loaded supply pallet: a vehicle load, not a pack load.
uses: Bulky: carried in both hands (Left Ctrl > Pick up)
A vehicle can take it in its hold if there is room

items.name: Zip Cuffs
items.desc: Plastic restraints for detaining people.
uses: Left Ctrl on a person > Zip-cuff: takes 3 s and uses one
Works from behind, or once they give up or are down; an armed hostile who sees you coming can't be cuffed
Moving or being interrupted stops it

items.name: Laptop (intel)
items.desc: An enemy laptop: the most valuable intel you can find.
uses: Found on people (Left Ctrl > Search for intel) or where a mission places it
Carry it out: at the debrief turn it in for a lead (a new, better-informed contract) or sell it to a faction
Worth about $3,000

items.name: Phone (intel)
items.desc: An enemy phone holding contacts and messages.
uses: Found on people (Left Ctrl > Search for intel) or where a mission places it
Carry it out: at the debrief turn it in for a lead or sell it to a faction
Worth about $1,200

items.name: Documents (intel)
items.desc: Papers taken from the enemy: orders, lists, maps.
uses: Found on people (Left Ctrl > Search for intel) or where a mission places it
Carry it out: at the debrief turn it in for a lead or sell it to a faction
Worth about $800

items.name: USB Drive (intel)
items.desc: A memory stick off an enemy or found where a mission places it: files worth something to a buyer.
uses: Found on people (Left Ctrl > Search for intel) or where a mission places it
Carry it out: at the debrief turn it in for a lead or sell it to a faction
Worth about $600

items.name: Ledger (intel)
items.desc: A handwritten account book: payments, names and dates, worth more than a phone's contacts.
uses: Found on people (Left Ctrl > Search for intel) or where a mission places it
Carry it out: at the debrief turn it in for a lead or sell it to a faction
Worth about $1,800

items.name: Smuggled Cigarettes
items.desc: A carton crate of untaxed cigarettes, the smugglers' bread and butter.
uses: Contraband: found at checkpoints, compounds and HQs
A shady fixer (Mama Rook) pays full price and thinks better of the company
Sold at the base it fetches 40%, and lawful employers think less of the company
Worth about $300

items.name: Captagon Pills
items.desc: A bag of captagon tablets: the militias' fuel and their cash crop.
uses: Contraband: found at checkpoints, compounds and HQs
A shady fixer (Mama Rook) pays full price and thinks better of the company
Sold at the base it fetches 40%, and lawful employers think less of the company
Worth about $2,500

items.name: Counterfeit Dollars
items.desc: Bundles of good fake hundreds, not good enough for a bank.
uses: Contraband: found at checkpoints, compounds and HQs
A shady fixer (Mama Rook) pays full price and thinks better of the company
Sold at the base it fetches 40%, and lawful employers think less of the company
Worth about $1,800

items.name: Unregistered Weapons Crate
items.desc: A crate of rifles with the serials ground off, on its way to whoever pays.
uses: Contraband: found at checkpoints, compounds and HQs
Heavy: 18 kg
A shady fixer (Mama Rook) pays full price and thinks better of the company
Sold at the base it fetches 40%, and lawful employers think less of the company
Worth about $3,500

items.name: HQ Strongbox Key
items.desc: A heavy key on a lanyard, carried by an HQ's officer: it opens that HQ's strongbox.
uses: Take it off the HQ's officer (his body)
Carry it to the HQ's strongbox and loot the box: the key opens it
Mission-only: worth nothing outside the zone

items.name: Old Key
items.desc: A worn key with a paper tag. Somewhere in this zone is the box it opens (Contractor: Fallen).
uses: Carry it to the locked box it belongs to and loot the box: the key opens it
A crowbar opens the same box without it, slowly and loudly

items.name: Dog Tags
items.desc: A fallen squadmate's identity tags, taken off his body: his name, callsign and role.
uses: Left Ctrl on a fallen squadmate's body > Take dog tags
Carry them out at extraction: he is recorded killed in action, his death benefit is paid and his name goes on the memorial wall with his tags recovered
Without his tags or his body he is missing in action until he's declared dead
Not for sale

items.name: Vantage Ledger (intel)
items.desc: A Vantage Group field ledger: payments, names and where their teams go. Evidence of what the rival PMC is really doing out here.
uses: Carried by a Vantage team's leader; sometimes in an HQ strongbox
Turn it in at the debrief like any intel: it opens a lead on the board
Or sell it to another faction

items.name: Cash Bundle
items.desc: A banded stack of bills, found in a cache or off a dead drop.
uses: Found where a mission places it, or out in the world (a cache, a wreck, a dead drop)
Carry it out and sell it at the base
Worth about $1,400

items.name: Gold Bars
items.desc: Small bullion bars: heavy for their size, worth a lot to the right buyer.
uses: Found where a mission places it, or out in the world (a cache, a wreck, a dead drop)
Carry it out and sell it at the base
Heavy for its size: 3 kg each
Worth about $2,800

items.name: Jewelry Case
items.desc: A locked case of jewelry, looted or left behind in a hurry.
uses: Found where a mission places it, or out in the world (a cache, a wreck, a dead drop)
Carry it out and sell it at the base
Worth about $2,200

items.name: Smuggled Relic
items.desc: An antiquity someone was moving through the region: the rarest find out in the field.
uses: Found where a mission places it, or out in the world (a cache, a wreck, a dead drop)
Carry it out and sell it at the base
Worth about $4,200

items.name: Copper Scrap
items.desc: Wiring and fittings stripped for their copper.
uses: Carry it out and it goes to the company stash
Left in the field it counts toward the debrief's salvage pool
Found in caches and wrecks out in the world

items.name: Machine Parts
items.desc: Precision-machined parts salvaged from equipment or a wreck.
uses: Carry it out and it goes to the company stash
Left in the field it counts toward the debrief's salvage pool
Found in caches and wrecks out in the world

items.name: Jerrycan (20 L fuel)
items.desc: A 20 L jerrycan of fuel.
uses: At a vehicle, Left Ctrl > Refuel (jerrycan): about 8 s
Heavy: 19 kg

items.name: Spare Wheel
items.desc: A spare wheel for a wheeled vehicle.
uses: At a wheeled vehicle, Left Ctrl > Spare Wheel: wheels: adds half the wheels' health back, about 25 s
Bulky: carried in both hands

items.name: Track Links
items.desc: Spare track links for a tracked vehicle.
uses: At a tracked vehicle, Left Ctrl > Track Links: tracks: repairs the tracks fully, about 45 s

items.name: Vehicle Repair Kit
items.desc: A general vehicle tool kit.
uses: At a vehicle, Left Ctrl > Vehicle Repair Kit: patches the engine, wheels, fuel tank or hull up to 60%, about 30 s

items.name: Vehicle Battery
items.desc: A replacement vehicle battery.
uses: At a vehicle with a dead battery, Left Ctrl > Vehicle Battery: battery: about 10 s

items.name: Engine Parts
items.desc: A set of engine parts.
uses: At a vehicle, Left Ctrl > Engine Parts: engine: repairs the engine fully, about 60 s
Salvaging a vehicle wreck yields a set

items.name: .50 BMG Belt (100)
items.desc: A 100-round belt of .50 BMG for a vehicle's M2 machine gun.
uses: Load it into the vehicle's hold (Left Ctrl at the vehicle); the M2 .50 cal feeds from belts in the hold
Heavy: 15 kg a belt

items.name: 12.7x108 Belt (50)
items.desc: A 50-round belt of 12.7x108 mm for a DShK machine gun.
uses: Load it into the vehicle's hold (Left Ctrl at the vehicle); the DShK feeds from belts in the hold

items.name: 120 mm M829A3 (APFSDS-T)
items.desc: One complete 120 mm M829A3 sabot round for the Abrams' M256: the tank-killer.
uses: At the Abrams' cargo point, Left Ctrl > Rearm: stowed in the bustle (then the hull rack), 10 s, the tank stopped
Heavy: 21 kg, carried in both hands; a pallet or a truck's hold moves them by the dozen

items.name: 120 mm M830A1 (HEAT-MP-T)
items.desc: One complete 120 mm M830A1 multi-purpose HEAT round: light armour, bunkers and helicopters.
uses: At the Abrams' cargo point, Left Ctrl > Rearm: 10 s, the tank stopped
Heavy: 24 kg, carried in both hands

items.name: 120 mm M1147 (AMP)
items.desc: One complete 120 mm M1147 advanced multi-purpose round: point detonating, delay or airburst against infantry and walls.
uses: At the Abrams' cargo point, Left Ctrl > Rearm: 10 s, the tank stopped
Heavy: 23 kg, carried in both hands

items.name: 25 mm M791 APDS-T (50, linked)
items.desc: A can of 50 linked 25 mm M791 armour-piercing rounds for the Bradley's M242 Bushmaster.
uses: At the Bradley's cargo point, Left Ctrl > Rearm: into the hull's stowage, 15 s a can, the vehicle stopped; the crew refills the ready boxes from there
Heavy: 30 kg a can

items.name: 25 mm M919 APFSDS-T (50, linked)
items.desc: A can of 50 linked 25 mm M919 depleted-uranium sabot rounds: the Bradley's AP feed takes them with the M919 package fitted.
uses: At the Bradley's cargo point, Left Ctrl > Rearm: 15 s a can
Fired only with the Bradley M919 ammo package fitted at the motor pool; otherwise the feed keeps M791

items.name: 25 mm M792 HEI-T (50, linked)
items.desc: A can of 50 linked 25 mm M792 high-explosive incendiary rounds for the M242.
uses: At the Bradley's cargo point, Left Ctrl > Rearm: 15 s a can, the vehicle stopped
Heavy: 31 kg a can

items.name: BGM-71E TOW-2A missile
items.desc: A TOW-2A wire-guided anti-tank missile in its launch tube, for the Bradley's twin launcher.
uses: At the Bradley's cargo point, Left Ctrl > Rearm: into the hull's TOW rack, 30 s, the vehicle stopped; a dismount reloads the launcher from there
Heavy: 29 kg, carried in both hands

items.name: 40 mm M430A1 HEDP (48, linked)
items.desc: A can of 48 linked 40 mm HEDP grenades for a Mk19 grenade machine gun (the AAV-7's weapon station).
uses: Stowed in a Mk19's racks once the AAV's weapon station fires them (F-244)
Heavy: 28 kg a can

items.name: Smoke Grenade Salvo (vehicle)
items.desc: One salvo's reload of multispectral smoke grenades for an armoured vehicle's dischargers (the Abrams' M250, the Bradley's M257).
uses: At the vehicle's cargo point, Left Ctrl > Rearm: into the dischargers' stowage, 10 s, the vehicle stopped
The crew reloads the dischargers from the stowage

items.name: Driver's Periscope
items.desc: A spare vision block and night periscope for an armoured vehicle's driver.
uses: At the vehicle's service point, Left Ctrl > Repair: swaps a damaged or broken driver's periscope, 30 s (two men; alone twice as long)

items.name: Reactive Armour Tile
items.desc: A spare explosive reactive armour tile (ARAT on the Abrams, BRAT on the Bradley), carried in the hold as a spare.
uses: At the vehicle's service point, Left Ctrl > Repair: replaces a tile that fired, 40 s (two men; alone twice as long)
Heavy: 28 kg, carried in both hands

items.name: Slat Armour Panel
items.desc: A spare bar-armour panel for a vehicle's slat kit.
uses: At the vehicle's service point, Left Ctrl > Repair: replaces a panel torn off, 40 s (two men; alone twice as long)
Bulky: carried in both hands

items.name: Ammunition Pallet (120 mm)
items.desc: A pallet of twelve 120 mm tank rounds: too heavy to carry, moved by a truck's hold or set down by helicopter.
uses: Within 8 m of an Abrams, Left Ctrl at its cargo point > Rearm from the pallet: each round at hand speed
At a truck's cargo point: Load the pallet into its hold; Cargo > take it sets it down by the truck

items.name: Ammunition Pallet (25 mm)
items.desc: A pallet of twelve cans of linked 25 mm (four M791, eight M792).
uses: Within 8 m of a Bradley, Left Ctrl at its cargo point > Rearm from the pallet
At a truck's cargo point: Load the pallet into its hold

items.name: Missile Pallet (TOW)
items.desc: A pallet of six TOW-2A missiles in their tubes.
uses: Within 8 m of a Bradley, Left Ctrl at its cargo point > Rearm from the pallet
At a truck's cargo point: Load the pallet into its hold

items.name: Smoke Salvo Pallet
items.desc: A pallet of twelve vehicle smoke grenade salvos.
uses: Within 8 m of an Abrams or a Bradley, Left Ctrl at its cargo point > Rearm from the pallet
At a truck's cargo point: Load the pallet into its hold

items.name: Fuel Drum Pallet (4 x 208 L)
items.desc: Four 208 L drums of diesel on a pallet, with a hand pump.
uses: Within 8 m of a vehicle, Left Ctrl at its cargo point > Refuel from the drums: 60 L a minute
At a truck's cargo point: Load the pallet into its hold (it pumps from there too)

items.name: 125 mm 3BM42 (APFSDS)
items.desc: A 125 mm 3BM42 sabot projectile with its charge, from an Eastern tank's carousel.
uses: Found in enemy armour's racks: salvage, worth money to the company
Heavy: 20 kg, carried in both hands

items.name: 125 mm 3OF26 (HE-FRAG)
items.desc: A 125 mm 3OF26 high-explosive round with its charge, from an Eastern tank.
uses: Found in enemy armour's racks: salvage
Heavy: 33 kg, carried in both hands

items.name: 30 mm 3UBR8 APDS-T (50, linked)
items.desc: 50 linked 30 mm 3UBR8 armour-piercing rounds for a 2A42 or 2A72 autocannon (BMP-2, BTR-82A).
uses: Found in enemy armour's racks: salvage
Heavy: 27 kg a belt

items.name: AT4 (M136) 84 mm
items.desc: A single-shot 84 mm disposable anti-armour launcher, loaded with a HEAT round.
uses: Launcher slot; 3 brings it up, right mouse aims (iron sight), Fire shoots
One shot: the tube is spent once fired
Backblast: lethal within 5 m behind you, injures to 30 m; a wall within 2 m reflects it
Can ride on a backpack's pack-top point

items.name: RPG-7
items.desc: A reloadable 40 mm launcher that fires 85 mm PG-7 rockets.
uses: Launcher slot; 3 brings it up, right mouse aims (optic), Fire shoots
R reloads (about 4.5 s) with a PG-7V (anti-armour) or OG-7V (fragmentation) rocket
Backblast: lethal within 4 m behind you, injures to 20 m

items.name: PG-7V HEAT rocket
items.desc: A PG-7V HEAT rocket for the RPG-7: anti-armour.
uses: Load into an RPG-7 (R with it up)
Shaped charge: about 260 mm of armour; needs 5 m to arm; self-destructs after 4.5 s of flight

items.name: OG-7V fragmentation rocket
items.desc: An OG-7V fragmentation rocket for the RPG-7: anti-personnel.
uses: Load into an RPG-7 (R with it up)
Blast and fragments out to about 15 m; no armour penetration

items.name: Javelin Command Launch Unit
items.desc: The Javelin command launch unit: a guided anti-armour system that locks onto vehicles.
uses: Launcher slot; 3 brings it up. Right mouse looks through the seeker; hold it on a vehicle for 2.5 s to lock (out to 2,500 m), then Fire
F switches top attack (climbs and dives onto the roof) and direct attack
R loads a Javelin missile (about 8 s)
Soft launch: backblast only within about 6 m

items.name: Javelin missile (launch tube)
items.desc: A Javelin missile in its launch tube: tandem HEAT, about 750 mm of armour.
uses: Load into the Javelin CLU (R with it up)
Needs 25 m to arm; flies to the locked target
Heavy and bulky: 16 kg

items.name: MAAWS (M3E1 Carl Gustaf) 84 mm
items.desc: The M3E1 84 mm recoilless rifle: reloadable, with rounds for armour, troops and buildings.
uses: Launcher slot; 3 brings it up, right mouse aims (optic), Fire shoots
R reloads (about 4 s) with FFV551 HEAT, FFV441 HE or FFV502 HEDP
Backblast: lethal within 5 m behind you, injures to 30 m

items.name: FFV551 HEAT round (84 mm)
items.desc: An FFV551 HEAT round for the MAAWS: anti-armour.
uses: Load into a MAAWS (R with it up)
About 450 mm of armour; needs 20 m to arm

items.name: FFV441 HE round (84 mm)
items.desc: An FFV441 high-explosive round for the MAAWS: anti-personnel.
uses: Load into a MAAWS (R with it up)
Blast and fragments out to about 20 m; no armour penetration

items.name: FFV502 HEDP round (84 mm)
items.desc: An FFV502 dual-purpose round for the MAAWS: some armour, good blast.
uses: Load into a MAAWS (R with it up)
About 150 mm of armour, fragments to about 12 m; good against buildings

items.name: NLAW
items.desc: A single-shot guided anti-armour launcher that leads a moving target.
uses: Launcher slot; 3 brings it up, right mouse aims, Fire shoots: it flies the predicted line of sight
F switches overfly top attack and direct attack
One shot: spent once fired; backblast only within about 5 m
Can ride on a backpack's pack-top point

items.name: SMAW (Mk153) 83 mm
items.desc: The Mk153 SMAW 83 mm assault launcher, for bunkers, buildings and light armour.
uses: Launcher slot; 3 brings it up, right mouse aims (optic), Fire shoots
R reloads (about 6 s) with a HEDP or thermobaric (NE) round
Backblast: lethal within 5 m behind you, injures to 25 m

items.name: SMAW HEDP round (Mk3)
items.desc: A SMAW HEDP round: dual-purpose, for light armour and walls.
uses: Load into a SMAW (R with it up)
About 200 mm of armour, fragments to about 10 m

items.name: SMAW-NE thermobaric round (Mk80)
items.desc: A SMAW-NE thermobaric round: a big blast for rooms and bunkers.
uses: Load into a SMAW (R with it up)
Large blast, little fragmentation, no armour penetration

items.name: Gen 1 NVG Monocular

stats._proposed: restores, fov_deg and battery_h are Proposed (wave 7, S2)

items.desc: An old first-generation night vision monocular: a grainy green picture through a narrow tube.
uses: Mount on your helmet (inventory), or press the NVG key (U) with a helmet on
NVG key flips it down or up; lowered, it shows you the dark in green
Gives back about 60% of what darkness takes from your sight
Battery: about 6 hours lowered; flat, it shows nothing

items.name: Gen 2 NVG Monocular

stats._proposed: restores, fov_deg and battery_h are Proposed (wave 7, S2)

items.desc: A second-generation night vision monocular: a clearer picture and a longer battery.
uses: Mount on your helmet (inventory), or press the NVG key (U) with a helmet on
NVG key flips it down or up; lowered, it shows you the dark in green
Gives back about 80% of what darkness takes from your sight
Battery: about 10 hours lowered; flat, it shows nothing

items.name: Gen 3 NVG Binocular

stats._proposed: restores, fov_deg and battery_h are Proposed (wave 7, S2)

items.desc: Third-generation binocular night vision: the clearest, widest picture, both eyes.
uses: Mount on your helmet (inventory), or press the NVG key (U) with a helmet on
NVG key flips it down or up; lowered, it shows you the dark in green
Gives back about 90% of what darkness takes from your sight
Battery: about 14 hours lowered; flat, it shows nothing

items.name: Vertical Foregrip
items.desc: A vertical foregrip for a railed rifle's handguard: a steadier hold on the gun.
uses: Mount on a railed rifle from the inventory (right-click > Mount on <gun>)
A fifth less recoil and a little less sway while aimed

items.name: Weapon Light
items.desc: A bright weapon-mounted flashlight for a rifle's or pistol's rail.
uses: Mount on a rifle or pistol from the inventory (right-click > Mount on <gun>)
L switches it on and off with the gun in hand (or right-click the gun > Switch on)
Lights up what you aim at, but anyone it points at sees you much sooner

items.name: Visible Laser
items.desc: A red aiming laser for a rifle's or pistol's rail: a dot where the gun points.

items.name: Fishing Rod
items.desc: A telescopic rod with line, hooks and a tin of weights.
uses: Survival: at the coast, a river, a lake or the dam, fish for a while (Migration.server_fish)
What bites depends on the water and the season

items.name: Fishing Net
items.desc: A small gill net with floats and sinkers.
uses: Survival: set at the water it takes two and a half times a rod's catch (Migration.server_fish)

items.name: Firewood
items.desc: Split logs. Green wood smokes and hisses: it wants a few days to season.
uses: Survival: from felling a tree (Trees); burns in a fire or a stove
Seasoned after a few world days (its state's cut day: Trees.seasoned)

items.name: Wool Beanie
items.desc: A knitted watch cap that pulls down over the ears.
uses: Survival: wear it in the head slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Keeps a little heat in your head

items.name: Baseball Cap
items.desc: A faded cap with a stiff peak: keeps the sun and the rain out of your eyes.
uses: Survival: wear it in the head slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Barely warm, but better than nothing

items.name: Trapper Hat
items.desc: A fur-lined hat with ear flaps that tie under the chin.
uses: Survival: wear it in the head slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
A real winter find: the warmest thing for your head

items.name: Wool Scarf
items.desc: A long knitted scarf, wound twice round the neck.
uses: Survival: wear it in the face slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Keeps the wind off your neck and frost off your face

items.name: Cotton T-Shirt
items.desc: A plain cotton T-shirt. Cotton soaks and stays cold when wet.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso base slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Base layer: next to the skin

items.name: Thermal Undershirt
items.desc: A long-sleeved waffle-knit thermal top.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso base slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Base layer: much warmer than cotton under the rest

items.name: Flannel Shirt
items.desc: A checked flannel work shirt with two chest pockets.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso mid slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Mid layer, with two small pockets
Its pockets add 0.3 L to your pockets

items.name: Hooded Sweatshirt
items.desc: A heavy cotton hoodie with a front pouch pocket.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso mid slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Mid layer, with a pouch pocket
Its pockets add 0.6 L to your pockets

items.name: Wool Sweater
items.desc: A thick oiled-wool jumper. Wool stays warm even damp.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso mid slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Mid layer: the warmest one you'll find

items.name: Fleece Jacket
items.desc: A zip-up fleece with two hand pockets.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso mid slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Mid layer, warm and light, with pockets
Its pockets add 0.6 L to your pockets

items.name: Rain Jacket
items.desc: A bright nylon shell with a hood. Keeps the rain off; rustles with every step.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso outer slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Outer layer: rain runs off it instead of soaking you
Loud: it raises the noise of your steps
Its pockets add 0.6 L to your pockets

items.name: Denim Jacket
items.desc: A stiff denim jacket with chest and hand pockets.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso outer slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Outer layer: tough, a little warmth, pockets
Its pockets add 0.6 L to your pockets

items.name: Field Jacket
items.desc: A woodland-pattern military field jacket with four big pockets.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso outer slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Outer layer: warm, sheds some rain, blends into woods, lots of pockets
Its pockets add 1.4 L to your pockets

items.name: Hunting Jacket
items.desc: A soft brushed hunting jacket in leaf camo, made to be quiet.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso outer slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Outer layer: quiet, blends into woods, pockets
Its pockets add 1.0 L to your pockets

items.name: Winter Parka
items.desc: A down-filled parka with a fur-trimmed hood: the find of a winter.
uses: Survival: wear it in the torso outer slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Outer layer: by far the warmest thing to wear
Big pockets; a little noisy
Its pockets add 1.6 L to your pockets

items.name: Wool Gloves
items.desc: Knitted gloves. Warm, but no grip when wet.
uses: Survival: wear it in the hands slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Keeps frost off your hands

items.name: Work Gloves
items.desc: Leather-palmed work gloves.
uses: Survival: wear it in the hands slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Keeps frost off your hands

items.name: Jeans
items.desc: Worn blue jeans with four pockets. Denim is cold and heavy when wet.
uses: Survival: wear it in the legs slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Legs, with pockets
Its pockets add 0.8 L to your pockets

items.name: Cargo Trousers
items.desc: Ripstop trousers with thigh cargo pockets.
uses: Survival: wear it in the legs slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Legs, with big cargo pockets
Its pockets add 1.4 L to your pockets

items.name: Insulated Snow Pants
items.desc: Padded, waterproof bib trousers.
uses: Survival: wear it in the legs slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Legs: warm and dry in snow; a little swishy
Its pockets add 0.4 L to your pockets

items.name: Rain Trousers
items.desc: Nylon over-trousers.
uses: Survival: wear it in the legs slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Legs: rain runs off
Loud: they rustle

items.name: Sneakers
items.desc: Soft running shoes: quiet, but they wear out and soak through.
uses: Survival: wear it in the feet slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Feet: quiet steps

items.name: Work Boots
items.desc: Steel-toed leather boots.
uses: Survival: wear it in the feet slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Feet: tough and fairly dry; a little louder

items.name: Winter Boots
items.desc: Felt-lined winter boots.
uses: Survival: wear it in the feet slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Feet: warm and dry in snow

items.name: Rubber Boots
items.desc: Knee-high rubber wellies.
uses: Survival: wear it in the feet slot (the gear editor, or pick it up with the slot free)
Feet: wade without getting your feet wet

items.name: Gun Cleaning Kit
items.desc: A pouch of rods, brushes, patches and solvent.
uses: Survival: right-click > Use cleans the gun in your hands (else your most worn one): about 20 s, +30 condition up to 85%
With a Gun Oil carried (one used) +50 and up to 100%; dries a wet gun and frees a jam
Ten cleanings in a kit

items.name: Gun Oil
items.desc: A small bottle of light gun oil.
uses: Survival: used with a Gun Cleaning Kit it brings a gun back to full
Right-click > Use on its own: a quick wipe (dries it, +8 condition)
Crafted from engine oil (firearms 1)

items.name: Gun Repair Kit
items.desc: Springs, pins, an extractor and a firing pin with the tools to fit them.
uses: Survival: right-click > Use repairs a broken gun you carry (firearms 2): about 40 s, back to 45% and firing
Used up

items.name: Whetstone
items.desc: A two-sided sharpening stone.
uses: Survival: right-click > Use sharpens the blade in your hands (else your dullest): about 8 s, +50 condition
A dull blade hits softer and a worn axe fells slower

items.name: Needle and Thread
items.desc: A sewing kit: needles and a spool of heavy thread.
uses: Survival: right-click > Use mends the most worn thing you wear: about 15 s, +35 condition
Torn clothes keep less warmth and shed less rain; worn-out boots make sore feet
Made from rags and copper wire (crafting)

items.name: Tyre Patch Kit
items.desc: Rubber patches, glue and a plug tool.
uses: Survival: right-click > Use by a vehicle with a flat (within 5 m) patches it: about 25 s
A flat holds a vehicle to 40% of its speed

items.name: Animal Bones
items.desc: Long bones off a butchered carcass, scraped clean.
uses: Survival: butchered from a kill (the context key on a carcass)
For tools, glue and broth when those come in

items.name: Animal Fat
items.desc: A lump of rendered fat from a kill: a lot of food in a little space.
uses: Right-click > Eat in the inventory (or double-click it)
Survival: 900 kcal of fat; keeps about a week, longer in the cold

items.name: Hand Line
items.desc: A spool of line on a stick with a few bent hooks.
uses: Survival: fish from the bank (the context key looking at water), worse than a rod
Made from copper wire and a stick

items.name: Salt
items.desc: A tub of table or rock salt.
uses: Survival: salt raw meat or fish (crafting) and it keeps for months
Found in kitchens and shops

items.name: Salted Meat
items.desc: Meat packed in salt until it's hard: salty, chewy, and it keeps.
uses: Right-click > Eat in the inventory (or double-click it)
Survival: about 280 kcal; keeps two months

items.name: Salted Fish
items.desc: Split fish in a crust of salt.
uses: Right-click > Eat in the inventory (or double-click it)
Survival: about 190 kcal; keeps six weeks

items.name: Dried Meat
items.desc: Thin strips of meat dried hard on a rack in the wind and sun.
uses: Right-click > Eat in the inventory (or double-click it)
Survival: about 260 kcal; light, and keeps six weeks

items.name: Dried Fish
items.desc: Fish split and dried on a rack until it rattles.
uses: Right-click > Eat in the inventory (or double-click it)
Survival: about 180 kcal; keeps a month

items.name: Block of Ice
items.desc: A slab cut from a frozen pond or river.
uses: Survival: cut in winter from frozen water (the context key looking at the ice)
In the settlement's stores an ice box keeps food cold (a block lasts two days out of winter)

items.name: Gun Parts
items.desc: A receiver group, a bolt, a barrel and springs off a stripped gun: what a gunsmith rebuilds from.
uses: Survival: stripped off a broken gun at a gunsmith bench (firearms 7)
A gunsmith bench rebuilds a broken gun from them (firearms 8): 1 a pistol, 2 a long gun, 3 a heavy one
Found on stripped guns, gun shops, police stations and armouries

items.name: Oil Filter
items.desc: A car's spin-on oil filter: a steel can packed with baffled paper.
uses: Survival: with a length of pipe it makes an improvised suppressor at a gunsmith bench (firearms 6)
Found in vehicle sheds, garages and wrecks

items.name: Oil-Filter Suppressor
items.desc: An oil filter on a threaded length of pipe: it quiets a gun for a few magazines, then it's shot through.
uses: Threaded muzzle: right-click it in the inventory > Mount on this gun
Wears out: about 60 shots, then it's gone
Made at a gunsmith bench from an oil filter and a pipe (firearms 6)

items.name: Reloading Press
items.desc: A single-stage press with dies: sizes the brass, seats the primer and the bullet.
uses: Survival: carried to a gunsmith bench, hand-loads ammunition from brass, primers, powder and lead (firearms 7)
Kept: not used up

items.name: Spent Brass
items.desc: Fired cases, dented but whole enough to load again.
uses: Survival: hand-loading at a gunsmith bench with a reloading press (firearms 7)

items.name: Primers (100)
items.desc: A flat of small primers: the hardest part of a reload to make.
uses: Survival: hand-loading at a gunsmith bench with a reloading press (firearms 7): one flat loads a batch

items.name: Smokeless Powder
items.desc: A pound tin of smokeless powder. Keep it dry and away from the fire.
uses: Survival: hand-loading at a gunsmith bench with a reloading press (firearms 7)

items.name: Lead Scrap
items.desc: Wheel weights and sinkers: cast into bullets and shot.
uses: Survival: hand-loading at a gunsmith bench with a reloading press (firearms 7)

items.name: Pipe Shotgun
items.desc: Two lengths of pipe, a nail for a firing pin and tape: one 12 gauge shell at a time. Loud, crude and not to be trusted.
uses: Primary slot; 1 brings it up
Single shot: R loads one standard or hi-brass shell
Improvised: it wears three times as fast, misfires more as it wears (the shell's lost) and at 0% it may blow up in your hands
Made at a gunsmith bench (firearms 7): the better the smith, the better it starts

items.name: Slam-Fire Shotgun
items.desc: A pipe sliding in a pipe over a fixed pin, a second shell taped to the stock: slam it home and it fires.
uses: Primary slot; 1 brings it up
Two shells: R loads standard or hi-brass shells one by one
Improvised: it wears three times as fast, misfires more as it wears (the shell's lost) and at 0% it may blow up in your hands
Made at a gunsmith bench (firearms 8)

items.name: Crude SMG
items.desc: An open-bolt 9 mm made from tube, sheet and a pistol's magazine: it sprays, and it's honest about it.
uses: Primary slot; 1 brings it up
Semi or full auto: F switches fire mode
Takes 9mm Magazines (17); R reloads in about 2.4 s
No rail: iron sights only
Improvised: it wears three times as fast, misfires more as it wears and at 0% it may blow up in your hands
Made at a gunsmith bench (firearms 9)
